newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds seen exploring topside of recent ranges.
newsitem.headline: Bunds seen exploring topside of recent ranges.

text.p: Bund futures rebounded from losses on Friday, finding support in firmer Treasuries and growing indications the Bundesbank will not tighten monetary policy this week.
The DTB Bund future was up 10 basis points in morning trade at 102.25, having traded in an early range between 102.19 and 102.38.
Traders said the upmove should be seen in the context of a recent narrow trading range and they saw resistance for the contract at around 102.40/50 and support at 102.15 and eventually 102.00.

The strength of the mark and share market weakness are making it less likely the Bundesbank will tighten monetary policy at Tuesday's repo announcement or its council meeting on Thursday, traders said.
The cash benchmark Bund was also higher, trading at 102.44 compared with 102.34 on Friday to yield 5.66 percent.
Investors are nonetheless nervous about increasing their Bund holdings with share market weakness a worry and the U.S. maybe facing higher interest rates.
The Bund/Treasury spread tightened during the morning to 66 basis points from 77 basis points on Friday.
Traders also said the short-end of the yield curve could get a lift from investors moving out of stocks and parking funds in short-maturity debt.
They added they were reluctant to push prices too high ahead of the U.S. market open and July M3 data and the Ifo business sentiment index due later in the week.
